discussion_comments.comment_body: Agreed, and fixed in ecd266455. A missing session bus or missing watcher is rejected immediately by the bus daemon itself (ENOENT / ServiceUnknown), so the only way to reach the 250 ms timeout is a watcher that exists but is slow to answer (a busy plasmashell or gnome-shell). Quitting there would end sessions on a desktop that does have a tray, while hiding there is just the pre-existing behavior. A timeout now keeps the hide-to-tray path, the doc comment explains why, and the test was flipped to `slow_probe_keeps_the_tray_behavior`.

Not reproducible. `std::process::Child::kill` returns `Ok(())` when the child has already exited (std behavior since Rust 1.72; this crate already needs 1.85+ for `edition2024`), and `wait()` returns the cached status, so retry falls through to `*process = None` and respawns. Checked with the installed toolchain:

```
rustc 1.97.1
try_wait reaped: Some(ExitStatus(unix_wait_status(1792)))
kill() after reap -> Ok(())
wait() after reap -> Ok(ExitStatus(unix_wait_status(1792)))
```

The Windows std impl has the same guard (treats `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` on an exited handle as `Ok`).

Addressed in 74f6a0c4dd. Both installers now recheck the installed build epoch while holding the installation lock, immediately before replacing the executable. The native CLI exposes a build-epoch probe and releases publish a matching metadata sidecar for cross-target caches. Added a locked downgrade rejection test that confirms the existing executable remains unchanged.
